title: Add a knowledge base metadata filter
alt: Knowledge base test settings with the Filters section open and genre entered in the filter field.
readSteps: Find the Filters section under the knowledge base test configuration.
The filter field contains genre.
The operator list includes equals, does not equal, in, starts with, and numeric comparisons.
practicalLesson: Use the operator list to check a metadata expression before you run a knowledge base query.
limit: This is a static AWS documentation screenshot. Console labels can change. A metadata filter does not replace authorization.

title: Combine metadata filters in one group
alt: Knowledge base filter group with genre and year expressions joined by and.
readSteps: The first expression is genre = "entertainment".
The second expression is year > 2018.
The and control joins both expressions. The screen also shows + Add Group.
practicalLesson: Use multiple expressions in one group when every condition must match. The source says a group supports up to five filters.
limit: This is a static AWS documentation screenshot. Console labels and filter limits can change. A metadata filter does not replace authorization.

title: Change the filter operator
alt: Knowledge base filter group with the and operator menu open and and and or options visible.
readSteps: The connector menu is between two filter expressions.
The menu shows and and or.
The selected connector controls whether all or at least one expression must match.
practicalLesson: Check the connector before you run the query. It changes the Boolean meaning of the filters.
limit: This is a static AWS documentation screenshot. Console labels can change. A metadata filter does not replace authorization.

title: Add a second filter group
alt: Knowledge base filter configuration with a second group and the + Add Group control highlighted.
readSteps: The first group contains genre and year expressions.
The second group contains genre and author expressions.
The + Add Group control creates another group.
practicalLesson: Use a separate group when a query needs nested Boolean conditions. The source says a configuration supports up to five groups.
limit: This is a static AWS documentation screenshot. Console labels and filter limits can change. A metadata filter does not replace authorization.

title: Choose how filter groups combine
alt: Knowledge base filters with the outer AND menu open between two groups.
readSteps: The outer connector sits between two filter groups.
The menu shows AND and OR.
The group connector is separate from the connectors inside each group.
practicalLesson: Read the outer operator and each inner operator to verify the full filter logic.

alt: Knowledge base filter configuration with a filter remove control and a group remove control highlighted.

title: Read a nested filter example
alt: Knowledge base filter example with two groups and different operators inside each group.
readSteps: The first group requires genre = "entertainment" and year > 2018.
The second group matches genre cooking or sports and author starts with C.
The outer operator is OR.

title: Enable prompt caching in the playground
alt: Amazon Bedrock playground settings with Prompt caching enabled and View cache checkpoints visible.
readSteps: The setting label is Prompt caching.
The toggle is on in this screenshot.
The panel says prompts and model responses are saved in cache checkpoints.
The panel includes View cache checkpoints.
practicalLesson: Check model support and the current API path before you use this setting. Prompt caching reuses prompt content, not a final application answer.
limit: This is a static AWS documentation screenshot. Model support and console labels vary. The screenshot does not guarantee a cache hit.

title: Read prompt cache token metrics
alt: Amazon Bedrock playground metrics panel with cache read tokens and cache write tokens.
readSteps: The panel heading is Caching metrics.
The panel lists Cache read tokens.
The panel lists Cache write tokens.
Both values are zero in this example image.
practicalLesson: Inspect read and write token counts after each model response. Treat the values in this screenshot as example values.

title: Test an agent return-control action
alt: Amazon Bedrock agent test window asking for an example output from an action group before Submit.
readSteps: The test window shows the action group OrderManagementAction.
The function shown is GetOrderHistory with orderId order-123.
The form requests an Action group function output value.
The buttons are Ignore and Submit.
practicalLesson: When an agent returns control, enter a representative action result and submit it to continue the test.
